questions.subject: FRENCH
questions.topic: Causal clause and its consequence
questions.learningObjective: Identify the consequence of a causal clause
questions.stem: Dispatcher log: the train was late because the signal failed, so which clause states the cause?

options.text: The clause introduced by parce que states the cause
The main clause states the cause
The clause introduced by donc states the cause

questions.explanation: Parce que introduces the causal clause. The main clause carries the consequence, not the cause, so reversing them is the tempting error.

questions.topic: Purpose clause after afin que
questions.learningObjective: Choose the mood after afin que
questions.stem: Dispatcher log: the controller slowed the train afin que the passengers could board, so which mood follows afin que?

questions.explanation: Purpose clauses after afin que take the subjonctif. The indicatif would wrongly present the purpose as a fact.

Pourtant marks the contrast

questions.explanation: Bien que introduces a concession, reversing the causal reading. Parce que would keep the causal meaning instead.

questions.stem: Dispatcher log: 'si le signal marche, le train part' versus 'si le signal marchait, le train partirait', so what changes?

answer.exemplar: The first uses the indicative for a real condition, while the second uses the conditional for a hypothetical, so the mood shift changes a real possibility into an imagined scenario.

questions.explanation: Indicative marks a real condition; conditional marks a hypothetical. Swapping them changes the meaning from possible to imagined.

questions.subject: FRENCH
questions.topic: Subjonctif after impersonal expressions of judgement
questions.learningObjective: Use the subjonctif after il est dommage que

stimulus.body: The log notes: il est dommage que the train is late. The expression conveys a judgement, not a fact.

questions.stem: Which mood follows il est dommage que?

options.text: Use the imparfait after il est dommage que
Use the indicatif after il est dommage que
Use the conditional after il est dommage que
Use the subjonctif after il est dommage que

questions.explanation: Il est dommage que triggers the subjonctif. The indicatif would wrongly present the late train as a plain fact.

questions.subject: FRENCH
questions.topic: Reported speech with a verb of the future
questions.learningObjective: Identify the tense in a future reported clause
questions.stem: Dispatcher log: the controller will say the train is delayed, so which tense appears in the reported clause?

options.text: Use the future in the reported clause
options.misconception: repeats the future of the reporting verb

options.text: Use the present in the reported clause for a current fact
Use the conditionnel in the reported clause
Use the imparfait in the reported clause

questions.explanation: A future reporting verb keeps the reported clause in the present for a current fact. The conditionnel would wrongly shift it into a past frame.

questions.subject: FRENCH
questions.topic: Causal clause and its consequence
questions.learningObjective: Distinguish cause from result
questions.stem: Dispatcher log: the signal failed, donc the train stopped, so why is donc not a cause marker?

answer.exemplar: Donc introduces the result or consequence, not the cause, so 'le signal a tombe, donc le train s'est arrete' states what followed, not why it happened.

questions.explanation: Donc marks the consequence. Parce que or puisque would introduce the cause instead.

questions.subject: FRENCH
questions.topic: Purpose clause after afin que
questions.learningObjective: Form a purpose clause with afin que

stimulus.body: The log states that the controller slowed the train so that passengers could board safely. The purpose clause has a different subject.

questions.stem: Which conjunction introduces that purpose clause?

options.text: Use parce que for the purpose
Use pour with an infinitive
Use afin que for a purpose with a different subject
Use donc for the purpose

questions.explanation: Afin que introduces a purpose clause with a different subject. Pour with an infinitive is for same-subject purpose.

questions.topic: One word that changes what a sentence means
questions.learningObjective: Explain how ne...que limits meaning
questions.stem: Dispatcher log: 'il ne reste qu'un train' changes the meaning, so how does qu' affect it?

options.text: Qu' intensifies the statement

Qu' restricts the statement to one train

questions.explanation: Ne...que limits the statement to one item. It does not negate or intensify.

questions.subject: FRENCH
questions.topic: Purpose clause after afin que
questions.learningObjective: Choose the mood after afin que
questions.stem: Dispatcher log: the controller slowed the train afin que the passengers could board, so which mood follows afin que?

answer.exemplar: Afin que introduces a purpose clause and requires the subjonctif, so 'afin que les voyageurs puissent monter' uses the subjonctif rather than the indicatif.

questions.explanation: Purpose clauses after afin que take the subjonctif. The indicatif would wrongly present the purpose as a fact.

questions.subject: FRENCH
questions.topic: One word that changes what a sentence means
questions.learningObjective: Identify the word that flips sentence meaning

stimulus.body: The log records two entries: the train stopped because the signal failed, and the train stopped although the signal worked. One word changes the whole meaning.

questions.stem: Which word changes the sentence from cause to concession?

options.text: Parce que marks the cause
Donc marks the result
Bien que marks the concession
Pourtant marks the contrast

questions.explanation: Bien que introduces a concession, reversing the causal reading. Parce que would keep the causal meaning instead.
